questions.question: Name the four factors that affect the resistance of a wire and state how each one changes the resistance.
questions.expected_answer: Material (e.g. nichrome has more resistance than copper); length (longer, more resistance); thickness (thicker, less resistance); temperature (for metals, hotter, more resistance).

questions.question: Describe how to investigate the effect of length on the resistance of a nichrome wire, naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables.
questions.expected_answer: Connect a cell, switch and ammeter to a nichrome wire on a metre rule with crocodile clips; record the current for lengths of 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 cm, switching off between readings. Independent: length; dependent: current (resistance); controlled: material, thickness, temperature, cell.

questions.question: Explain, in terms of electrons and atoms, why heating a metal wire increases its resistance.
questions.expected_answer: When the metal is heated its atoms vibrate more strongly, so the moving electrons collide with them more often, which opposes their flow more, so the resistance increases.
